summary:
Ghosts of Space: The Machines That Never Came Home is an interactive digital space museum that explores the stories of NASA machines left behind on the Moon and Mars. Through an immersive 2.5D experience, visitors can discover eight historic space artifacts, explore their missions, understand their scientific contributions, and learn what happened to them after their journeys ended.

The experience features dedicated Moon and Mars explorations, archival NASA imagery, interactive artifact stories, and educational science experiences. Visitors can experiment with the Apollo 11 laser-ranging concept and explore how the InSight mission helped scientists study Marsquakes.

By transforming space exploration history into an engaging, accessible experience, Ghosts of Space aims to inspire curiosity, preserve the legacy of robotic and human exploration, and help people understand that even machines that never came home left behind discoveries that continue to shape our understanding of the universe.
details:
Ghosts of Space: The Machines That Never Came Home is an interactive digital space museum exploring abandoned and retired NASA equipment on the Moon and Mars.

The project presents eight historical artifacts through immersive Moon and Mars exploration pages, archival NASA photographs, mission timelines, scientific explanations, and interactive experiences. Visitors can explore the history and scientific contributions of machines such as the Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retro-Reflector, Surveyor 3, Sojourner rover, Mars Pathfinder, Phoenix, and InSight.

Two interactive experiences make the science more accessible: a laser-ranging experiment demonstrating the time light takes to travel between Earth and the Moon, and an InSight experience explaining how scientists study Marsquakes.

We developed the project using React, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Vite, and Google's <model-viewer> component for 3D planetary models. The interface combines archival imagery, animations, and responsive design to create a digital museum experience.

Our goal is to make space exploration history engaging and understandable, especially for students, while showing how scientific discoveries continue to matter long after missions end.
